title: Louis Armstrong's advice not to go South
summary: Armstrong warned Scott away from the South, and Scott never went further south than Richmond.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But, anyhow, I was telling you about going away to Europe. Well, I explained to Duke about my position. Louis Armstrong had told me, he said, Scottie, you're a city boy. You never been South, because I hadn't. He said, don't go South, because you wouldn't understand it.

He told me that. We were talking one day, like fellows do, just -- he said, don't go South because you wouldn't understand it. Well, to this day, I haven't been any further South than Richmond, Virginia. Because when I went to California, I went by the Northern route, around Cleveland and Chicago and all like that way. I haven't been South.
Because of what Louis said, or --

Yeah, well, he ought to know. He ought to know. We were good friends, because he used to write me and we used to exchange letters, even when he went to Europe. But he travelled -- when he got his own band, I lost connections with him. He couldn't keep up with travelling, and sometimes I'd be out of town myself.
